493: pub fn find_iter_at_in_context<M, F>(
494:     searcher: &Searcher,
495:     matcher: M,
496:     mut bytes: &[u8],
497:     range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
498:     mut matched: F,
499: ) -> io::Result<()>

501:     M: Matcher,
502:     F: FnMut(Match) -> bool,

504:     // This strange dance is to account for the possibility of look-ahead in
505:     // the regex. The problem here is that mat.bytes() doesn't include the
506:     // lines beyond the match boundaries in mulit-line mode, which means that
507:     // when we try to rediscover the full set of matches here, the regex may no
508:     // longer match if it required some look-ahead beyond the matching lines.
509:     //
510:     // PCRE2 (and the grep-matcher interfaces) has no way of specifying an end
511:     // bound of the search. So we kludge it and let the regex engine search the
512:     // rest of the buffer... But to avoid things getting too crazy, we cap the
513:     // buffer.
514:     //
515:     // If it weren't for multi-line mode, then none of this would be needed.
516:     // Alternatively, if we refactored the grep interfaces to pass along the
517:     // full set of matches (if available) from the searcher, then that might
518:     // also help here. But that winds up paying an upfront unavoidable cost for
519:     // the case where matches don't need to be counted. So then you'd have to
520:     // introduce a way to pass along matches conditionally, only when needed.
521:     // Yikes.
